en omkamp.explanation: "En omkamp" means "a rematch". It is built from "om" (again) and "en kamp" (a match). The part "om" also means "again" in "at lave om" (to redo): "Jeg laver opgaven om" (I redo the assignment).

en omkostning.explanation: "En omkostning" means "a cost". To talk about the costs of running something in the plural, say: "høje omkostninger" (high costs). To ask what one thing you buy costs, use "en pris" (a price): "Hvad er prisen?" (What is the price?)

en omkørsel.explanation: "En omkørsel" means "a detour". To tell someone to follow the route set up around a closed road, say: "Følg omkørslen" (Follow the detour). To say you choose a longer way yourself, use "en omvej" (a longer way): "Jeg tager en omvej hjem" (I take a longer way home).

en omlægning.explanation: "En omlægning" means "a restructuring". It comes from "at lægge om" (to change over): "Hun lægger kosten om" (She changes her diet). To say a loan gets new terms, say: "omlægning af lån" (switching a loan to new terms).

en omstilling.explanation: "En omstilling" means "an adjustment / a transition". To say a change takes getting used to, say: "en stor omstilling" (a big adjustment). To say you call a company, use "omstillingen" (the switchboard): "Jeg ringer til omstillingen" (I am calling the switchboard).

en omstændighed.explanation: "En omstændighed" means "a circumstance". To say you will do something whatever happens, say: "Jeg kommer under alle omstændigheder" (I will come in any case). To say how things are right now, say: "Under de omstændigheder" (Under the circumstances).

en omsætning.explanation: "En omsætning" means "a turnover / revenue". To say what a business has left after costs, use "en fortjeneste" (a profit): "Vi har en stor fortjeneste" (We have a large profit).

en omvej.explanation: "En omvej" means "a detour". To say you take a longer way, say: "Jeg tager en omvej" (I take a longer way). To say you take the shorter way, use "en genvej" (a shortcut): "Jeg tager en genvej" (I take a shortcut).

en onkel.explanation: "En onkel" means "an uncle". To use it as a title before a name, say: "onkel Peter" (Uncle Peter). Danish has separate words for an uncle on each side: "en morbror" (mother's brother) and "en farbror" (father's brother). To say where your father's brother lives, say: "Min farbror bor i Odense" (My father's brother lives in Odense).

en opdagelse.explanation: "En opdagelse" means "a discovery". To say someone found something that was already there, say: "Han gjorde en vigtig opdagelse" (He made an important discovery). To say a person made something new, use "en opfindelse" (an invention): "Hjulet er en gammel opfindelse" (The wheel is an old invention).

en opdatering.explanation: "En opdatering" means "an update". The verb is "at opdatere" (to update): "Jeg opdaterer appen" (I am updating the app).

en opdeling.explanation: "En opdeling" means "a division". It comes from "at dele op" (to split up): "Vi deler klassen op" (We split the class up).

en opdragelse.explanation: "En opdragelse" means "an upbringing". To describe how strict it was, say: "en streng opdragelse" (a strict upbringing). To talk about the years of growing up in a place, use "en opvækst" (an upbringing in a place): "en opvækst på landet" (growing up in the countryside).

en opera.explanation: "En opera" means "an opera". To say you go to the building, say: "Vi skal i operaen i aften" (We are going to the opera tonight). In Copenhagen, "Operaen" (the Opera House) is on the island of Holmen. To say you go to a play, use "et teater" (a theater): "Vi skal i teatret i aften" (We are going to the theater tonight).

en operation.explanation: "En operation" means "an operation", as in surgery at a hospital. The verb is "at operere" (to operate): "Lægen opererer hende" (The doctor is operating on her).

en opfattelse.explanation: "En opfattelse" means "a perception / view". To say what you think about a plan, say: "Min opfattelse er, at planen er for dyr" (My view is that the plan is too expensive). To ask what someone else thinks, say: "Hvad er din opfattelse?" (What is your view?)

en opfindelse.explanation: "En opfindelse" means "an invention". To say something was made long ago, say: "Hjulet er en gammel opfindelse" (The wheel is an old invention). To say someone found something that was already there, use "en opdagelse" (a discovery): "Han gjorde en vigtig opdagelse" (He made an important discovery).

en opfinder.explanation: "En opfinder" means "an inventor". It comes from "at opfinde" (to invent), and "-er" makes it the person who does it, just like in "en lærer" (a teacher). To say what someone is, say: "Hun er opfinder" (She is an inventor).

en opfordring.explanation: "En opfordring" means "a call / appeal". To say someone did something because they were asked, say: "Han sang på opfordring" (He sang when asked to).

en opførelse.explanation: "En opførelse" means "a construction / a performance". To say a big structure is built, use the first meaning: "opførelsen af en bro" (the construction of a bridge). To say a play is shown, use the second meaning: "opførelsen af en opera" (the performance of an opera). To say how someone behaves, use "en opførsel" (behavior): "Hans opførsel var uhøflig" (His behavior was rude).

en opgang.explanation: "En opgang" means "a stairwell / entrance". To say which entrance of an apartment block you live in, say: "Jeg bor i opgang B" (I live in stairwell B).

en opgave.explanation: "En opgave" means "a task". To say what you have to do at school, use it for an exercise: "en matematikopgave" (a math exercise). To say what you are asked to do at work, use it for a duty: "Jeg har en ny opgave" (I have a new task).

en opgavebog.explanation: "En opgavebog" means "an exercise book". It is built from "en opgave" (a task) and "en bog" (a book). To say you write the answers in it, say: "Jeg skriver i opgavebogen" (I am writing in the exercise book).

en opgivelse.explanation: "En opgivelse" means "a giving up". It comes from "at opgive" (to give up): "Han opgav drømmen" (He gave up the dream).

en opgørelse.explanation: "En opgørelse" means "a statement / a count". It comes from "at opgøre" (to work out): "Jeg opgør udgifterne" (I work out the expenses).
